DexYCB: A Benchmark for Capturing Hand Grasping of Objects
Hybrid Imitation Learning Framework for Robotic Manipulation Tasks
Learning Robot In-Hand Manipulation with Tactile Features

cited_details.statement: A study published in Robotics: Science and Systems reports that tactile sensors can be leveraged to estimate both the in-hand object pose of a grasped object and the contact location between the hand and object during non-prehensile manipulation tasks (https://www.roboticsproceedings.org/rss20/p135.pdf).

The cited work positions tactile-driven pose and contact estimation as an approach for non-prehensile manipulation, with the in-hand pose and contact location estimated directly from tactile sensors (https://www.roboticsproceedings.org/rss20/p135.pdf).

A study showed that a tactile manipulation skill can be successfully acquired using a passively compliant hand, with tactile features mapped to control actions during learning (https://users.cs.utah.edu/~thermans/papers/vanhoof-ichr2015-in-hand-learning.pdf).
Beyond real-robot systems, the DexYCB benchmark provides a standardized dataset for capturing hand grasping of objects (https://dex-ycb.github.io/).

The benchmark covers 2D object and keypoint detection, 6D object pose estimation, and 3D hand pose estimation, together with a robotics-relevant evaluation of generating safe robot grasps in human-to-robot object handover (https://dex-ycb.github.io/).

The authors of DexYCB first compare DexYCB with a related dataset through cross-dataset evaluation, then present a thorough benchmark of state-of-the-art approaches on the three perception tasks, before evaluating the handover task, with these steps together providing a structured evaluation protocol for the listed perception components (https://dex-ycb.github.io/).

The OpenAI study on learning dexterous in-hand manipulation uses RL to learn policies that can perform vision-based object manipulation with a dexterous hand (https://matthiasplappert.com/publications/2020_OpenAI_Dexterous-Manipulation_IJRR.pdf).

The cited abstract indicates that RL is the principal means by which the policy is obtained, with vision supplying the perceptual signal (https://matthiasplappert.com/publications/2020_OpenAI_Dexterous-Manipulation_IJRR.pdf).

A hybrid imitation learning (HIL) framework has been proposed in which behavior cloning (BC) and state cloning (SC) methods are combined within a single architecture for robotic manipulation tasks (https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/21/10/3409).
The cited abstract frames BC and SC as complementary components of the HIL architecture for robotic manipulation tasks (https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/21/10/3409).

The platform includes a simulation system for complex dexterous manipulation tasks with a multi-finger robot hand, and a computer vision system that records large-scale demonstrations of a human hand conducting the same tasks (https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.05877).

In the DexMV pipeline, 3D hand and object poses are extracted from videos and a novel demonstration translation method converts human motion to robot demonstrations (https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.05877).

The authors then apply and benchmark multiple imitation learning algorithms on the resulting dataset, and the cited abstract reports that the demonstrations improve robot learning by a large margin and enable the solution of complex tasks that reinforcement learning alone cannot solve (https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.05877).

The DexMV authors note that, despite significant progress on understanding hand-object interactions in computer vision, it is still very challenging for robots to perform complex dexterous manipulation, which is presented as the motivation for the DexMV platform (https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.05877).
The DexYCB benchmark presents evaluations on a defined set of perception and handover tasks and provides a benchmark of state-of-the-art approaches on those tasks (https://dex-ycb.github.io/).

The OpenAI RL study focuses on vision-based object manipulation with a dexterous hand, learning such policies using RL as the principal training mechanism (https://matthiasplappert.com/publications/2020_OpenAI_Dexterous-Manipulation_IJRR.pdf).
The HIL framework is described in the cited abstract as a novel architecture combining BC and SC for robotic manipulation tasks more broadly (https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/21/10/3409).
Tactile-driven state estimation addresses in-hand pose and contact recovery during non-prehensile manipulation (https://www.roboticsproceedings.org/rss20/p135.pdf).
RL provides a recipe for acquiring vision-based object manipulation policies with a dexterous hand (https://matthiasplappert.com/publications/2020_OpenAI_Dexterous-Manipulation_IJRR.pdf).
IL leverages human demonstrations to bootstrap complex multi-finger skills that RL alone cannot solve (https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.05877).
The DexYCB benchmark evaluates state-of-the-art approaches on 2D detection, 6D pose, 3D hand pose, and safe handover tasks (https://dex-ycb.github.io/).
The HIL framework combines behavior cloning and state cloning within a single architecture for robotic manipulation tasks (https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/21/10/3409).
Tactile features have been shown to support acquisition of a manipulation skill with a passively compliant hand (https://users.cs.utah.edu/~thermans/papers/vanhoof-ichr2015-in-hand-learning.pdf).
